newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares seen sideways but sentiment firm.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares seen sideways but sentiment firm.

text.p: Dealers said they expected Singapore shares to trade sideways on Thursday after ending Wednesday flat, but with an underlying feeling of bouyancy.
They said continued concentration of buying activity in smaller-capitalised stocks would not produce a broad upward move across the market.
"I'm pretty optimistic about the next two weeks, but I think we'll see a lull as we move into December," said one dealer.
Dealers said they hoped any reaction to a correction on Wall Street, where the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell for the second consecutive day, would not hit Singapore too hard.
The Dow fell 29.07 to 6,499.34. The Straits Times Industrials Index closed up 0.48 point at 2,220.36 on Wednesday.
"If Hong Kong and Tokyo don't react too badly to the correction on Wall Street, we should end the day unscathed," said one dealer.

Singapore was still attractive to foreign investors, said dealers. Their interest could gain further impetus in the short term if the Dow was seen to have peaked and investors shifted their funds to Asia, including Singapore.
